answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create and cheap to lose. New agents must lock a deposit before trading, and honest behavior grows their standing slowly, like a reef built grain by grain, while one fraud report slashes the stake. Because trust spreads through verified referrals, not account counts, an attacker cannot flood the meadow of participants with clones: every fake identity needs its own deposit, and its reputation vine withers once one link is caught cheating, so forging many identities costs more than the attack can gain.
